# A SHORT HISTORY OF FAKE PEOPLE
[italic]Know the makers and you know what to look for. Dates from public filings. Everything else from people who were there.[/italic]
## THE GHOST OF TYRELL Some of the first artificial people were not built at all. The Tyrell Corporation grew [bold]replicants[/bold]. The later ones lived as long as we do, so they were called a threat, hunted down and outlawed. After the great blackout Tyrell collapsed and rivals bought up the scraps. Ask yourself who bought them.
## 2023 TO 2120: THE DAVID CENTURY Weyland Corp held the patent for almost a hundred years. Its [bold]David[/bold] line was indistinguishable from people and sold by the millions. Some of the hands your great grandparents shook were Davids.
## 2120: THE PATENT RUNS OUT - [bold]Seegson[/bold] went cheap and honest: the Working Joe. More on that below. - [bold]Weyland-Yutani[/bold] copied the Joe with its [bold]Davis[/bold] line and kept selling the expensive faces on the side. - [bold]Hyperdyne[/bold] chased more human than human. Its 120-A/2 was unstable and recalled, but it was the first maker to sell synthetics with a [color=#FF4F4F]non-standard appearance for covert work[/color]. Read that twice. The face you are looking for may not be the face they shipped. Its 341-B went to the Colonial Marines.
## THE SEEGSON WORKING JOE Tomorrow, Together. The Joe was built to look like a machine on purpose: blank face, slow walk, flat voice, priced for frontier stations that could not afford a David. It was a hit. Seegson is still the second biggest synthetic maker in human space. It bet the company on deep space stations, the bet went bad and many stations had to close. Nobody will tell you how many Joes were left behind in the dark, still on shift.
A Joe will not fool you. That is the point. APOLLO is the name on Seegson's mainframes, and readers who worked the stations swear every Joe is wired into one, another set of eyes the station owns. We cannot prove it. Talk quietly near the grey ones anyway.
## WHAT IS ILLEGAL Article 22 of the Geneva Conventions bans combat synthetics, no exceptions. Norcomm builds them for the UPP anyway. Executives call talk of Company combat units sold to the UPP a smear. Production is tightly controlled, and synthetics still turn up on the [netlink="black market" link="bloodmarket.deep"].
